title: Forecast Collapse in Time-Series Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.14106v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: When forecasting hourly returns for 1,000 US equities, we observe an unexpected phenomenon: predictions become nearly flat and show poor stock ranking, as measured by cross-sectional correlation. We call this forecast collapse. Surprisingly, the phenomenon largely disappears when forecasting trading volume under the same setting. We investigate forecast collapse across time-series foundation models (TSFMs), twelve deep-learning forecasting models, and 97 public benchmark configurations, and find that it is closely tied to target predictability. We identify two distinct reasons behind it: low predictability limits the amplitude of calibrated point forecasts, while per-series objectives leave cross-series structure unidentified. translated_title: 时间序列基础模型中的预测崩溃现象
translated_abstract: 在对1000只美国股票的每小时收益率进行预测时，我们观察到一个意外现象：预测结果变得近乎平坦，且股票排名表现不佳，这一现象通过横截面相关性来衡量。我们将其称为“预测崩溃”。令人惊讶的是，在相同设置下预测交易量时，这一现象基本消失。我们研究了时间序列基础模型（TSFMs）、十二种深度学习预测模型以及97个公共基准配置中的预测崩溃现象，发现它与目标可预测性密切相关。我们识别出其背后的两个不同原因：低可预测性限制了校准点预测的幅度，而逐序列目标使得跨序列结构未被识别。这些发现揭示了一个校准与排名之间的权衡：优化平方误差会导致预测平坦化，而直接优化横截面相关性虽能改善排名，但可能夸大预测幅度。
tldr: 本文揭示了时间序列基础模型在预测股票收益时出现的“预测崩溃”现象，其根源在于低可预测性和逐序列目标设计，并指出了校准与排名之间的权衡关系。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals the "forecast collapse" phenomenon in time-series foundation models when predicting stock returns, rooted in low predictability and per-series objective design, and highlights the calibration-ranking tradeoff.
